subject: Eviction circuit-breaker playbook — backup purge & log window escalation
messages:
From: Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@medisync.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@medisync.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eviction circuit-breaker playbook — backup purge & log window escalation

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the call this morning. Medisync's audit team needs a short, machine-readable description of how Redwood would pause an automated backup purge if a legal or regulatory hold is detected in our tenant. Specifically:

- What signals are used to trigger a pause (API call, legal-hold flag, customer support ticket)?
- How long can a pause be maintained without manual intervention?
- Where are paused snapshots kept and who can approve re‑enablement?
- What audit evidence is emitted (events, timestamps, operator id)?

We're trying to map this into our DPA addendum appendix. Can you send a concise playbook and any sample audit extracts?

Best,
Sara
Sara Mendez
Head of Compliance, Medisync

--

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@medisync.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eviction circuit-breaker playbook — backup purge & log window escalation

Sara —

Appreciate the specificity. Attached is our proposed "Eviction Circuit-Breaker Playbook" (PDF) and a CSV with sample audit events. High level (quick bullets):

1) Trigger signals
   - Legal-Hold API: customers or Redwood Legal can set a tenant-level hold via the Private Control Plane API.
   - Support Escalation: creation of an Escalation ticket with the tag "preserve-data" triggers a soft‑pause.
   - Automated Detection: SOC webhook (for suspected forensics) can initiate a temporary hold (default 48 hours).

2) Pause semantics
   - Soft-Pause: stops scheduled purge jobs, retains new backups to a held snapshot bucket for up to 14 days before requiring escalation.
   - Hard-Pause (requires approval): moves snapshots to escrow storage (immutable bucket, region-scoped) and disables purge until approved. Hard‑pause can be retained for up to 90 days under the current runbook then reviewed quarterly.

3) Approvals & roles
   - Approvers: Customer Admin, Redwood Legal, and Redwood Ops (two-party approval for hard‑pause removal).
   - Read-only access: Security/Compliance teams can download audit evidence and snapshot indices.

4) Audit evidence
   - Every action emits an event: {timestamp, actor, signal_type, tenant_id, snapshot_ids, action_id}. See attached CSV sample.

Next steps: can we get Medisync's preferred retention windows for paused snapshots and whether you require onshore (US-only) escrow storage for hard‑pause snapshots?

I'll loop Kimberley on the DPA implications and Aditya on the ops automation.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Security Program Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-eviction-circuit-breaker.pdf, audit-evidence-list.csv

--

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@medisync.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eviction circuit-breaker playbook — backup purge & log window escalation

Sara —

Quick follow-up on the DPA language: two items Medisync should confirm to make the addendum precise:

• Onshore escrow: if you require US-only escrow, we need to annotate the DPA Annex stating "Held snapshots will be transferred to Redwood-managed US immutable storage (S3 — GovCloud equivalent)". That alters our subprocessor footprint — Aditya, note potential AWS GovCloud involvement.

• Maximum automatic hold duration: we propose a default hard‑pause maximum of 90 days with option for extension by exception (legal/ops signoff). If Medisync wants indefinite holds, we will need an administrative change request and acceptance of additional storage costs.

If Medisync confirms US-only and the 90‑day limit, we can propose a short DPA annex that references the playbook and the audit schema.

Kimberly Park
VP, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

--

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@medisync.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eviction circuit-breaker playbook — backup purge & log window escalation

Sara / team —

Operational notes from infra/ops perspective:

- Implementation: we implement the soft/hard pause by tagging scheduled purge jobs with tenant flags. Soft‑pause halts job execution; hard‑pause triggers a snapshot export to an immutable bucket and flips the tenant purge state to "ESCROWED".
- Cost & retention impact: soft‑paused snapshots are retained in normal region for 14 days (no extra cost). Hard‑pause snapshots require escrow storage and incur per‑GB/month. We will include a cost table in the annex.
- Rollback safety: when a hard‑pause is enacted we create a change ticket with an immutable audit id; any attempted purge action after that point is blocked by enforcement middleware.

Action items:
1) Sara: confirm whether Medisync wants US-only escrow and whether they will accept the 90‑day default.
2) Kimberly/Irene: I can prepare the ops sections for the DPA annex and the cost table once we have the escrow decision.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

--

From: Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@medisync.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eviction circuit-breaker playbook — backup purge & log window escalation

Team —

Thanks, everyone. Quick answers from Medisync: 

• US-only escrow: yes, required for the initial roll-out (we'll re-evaluate later).
• 90-day default: acceptable for now, but please include an extension process (Legal approval + cost estimate) in the annex.
• Audit extracts: the CSV sample you sent looks good; we need the event schema described in plain text to map to our internal SIEM.

Request: can you provide a short paragraph that we can drop into the DPA Addendum under "Emergency Retention & Purge Suspension"? Also we want one concrete example of an audit event (with real-looking fields) to validate ingestion.

If you can send that by Monday we'll share with our procurement and legal.

Best,
Sara
